claimed: issue-worker-high (Opus 5.5) · 2026-11-22T09:33Z · worktree/branch issue/3316-offset-pass-start · plan: dump each lateral rapid below Z32 in the fig8 pin run, find its source, fix on the #3316 branch if the cause is shared

Finding of the pin run, 2026-11-22. The cause of this issue is NOT shown to be shared with #3316. I release the claim.

What I did:
- Pin `crates/app/tests/offset_pass_start.rs` on branch `issue/3316-offset-pass-start` (not pushed yet). Model `testdata/models/fig8.step`, tool `EM-0800-4FL`, Outside containment over the floor face.
- Heights as reported: Clearance = Top of stock +10 (Z 32), Top = Top of stock +0 (Z 22), Bottom = Selection +1.5 (Z 1.5), Stepdown 10, `retract_z: None` (hop off). Entry Helix, radius 1.6. Links are `Links::PLANAR` (Between levels "Clearance plane", Between passes "Retract plane").
- The test lists each rapid with an XY move whose lower end is below Z 32. It also reads the verifier warnings for `RapidInStock`.

What the runs show:
- Stock box margins 0, 2, 5, 10 and 20 mm around the part, and stepovers 3 and 4: zero lateral rapids below Z 32, and zero `RapidInStock` warnings. This is true for the old order (Auto) and for the new Outside order.
- The only verifier warnings are `ShankHit` on the last level (Z 1.5). The catalog tool is shorter than the 20.5 mm depth.
- Our move counts (2154 to 4488) do not agree with the reported 1764 moves. So the reported operation has a setting that the pin does not have. The candidates are the stock shape and size, the tool assembly length, and a setting on the Lead in / Lead out tab other than the defaults.

A clue from the move numbers: with 3 levels and about 588 moves for each level, moves 543, (one more) and 1711 are near the END of each level. In the Auto order the end of each level is the outermost ring work. The "cuts past the finish surface" moves 522 to 1710 have the same position in each level.

The guard test `fig8_auto_offset_keeps_every_lateral_rapid_at_the_clearance_plane` stays in the #3316 PR. It does not reproduce this issue. A second worker needs the stock and tool data of the maintainer's `2D Offset1` (not the private project file) to reproduce it.

blocked: this issue needs the stock, tool and Lead in / Lead out values of the maintainer's operation `2D Offset1` (not the private project file).

The pin run of 2026-11-22 did not show the defect with the default values (see the comment before this one). The move count of the pin (2154 to 4488) does not agree with the reported 1764 moves, so one or more settings are different.

Values that are necessary:
- Stock: the shape, the size and the offsets.
- Tool: the assembly length and the holder.
- Lead in / Lead out tab: each value that is not the default.
- Passes tab: the stepover, and each finish or spring pass setting.

The main session asks the maintainer for these values. A scout reads the code for a lateral rapid at the end of a level in the meantime.

Findings from a read of the 2D Offset planner on `origin/main`. Nothing was built or run. Each item says if it is proven by reading or a hypothesis.

- Proven by reading: with "Hop below clearance" off, each planar lateral rapid is at the clearance plane. No path that was read posts a lateral rapid below the clearance. A keep-down link that succeeds posts no rapid.
- Proven by reading: each pass link posts a vertical rapid down (`descent_dive.rs:26-30`). The verifier judges a vertical drop by its column (`crates/sim/src/verify/rapids.rs:117-124`).
- Hypothesis: the three reported moves are vertical rapids into stock, not lateral rapids. The best candidate is the restart at the pass start in `ladder_links.rs:189-199`. It runs when the entry is not Plunge. It posts a lateral rapid at the clearance and then a vertical rapid down to the material top plus 2 mm (`descent.rs:352`, `descent_dive.rs:106-168`). It occurs one time for each level, which agrees with three moves.
- The level links (Helix from the level before) occur only two times for three levels.
- 2D Offset has no finish pass and no spring pass. The settings that change the move count are the stepover, the stock to leave, the containment and its offset, the corner relief and the blend turns.

To decide this, a move dump of the reported operation is necessary: for moves 543, about 1127 and 1711, the start point and the end point (X, Y, Z). If X and Y are equal at the two ends, the move is a vertical drop, and the question is which material top the drop uses.
